claims.text: Introducing uniformly dispersed CaF2 particles into CoCrFeNi will enable in situ formation of a stable lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
A CaF2-containing CoCrFeNi composite will maintain low friction and reduced wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy contains no self-lubricating secondary phases.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits increasing friction coefficient and wear rate as sliding temperature is varied from room temperature to 800 °C.
Approximately 3–5 wt% CaF2 can be incorporated into CoCrFeNi by powder metallurgy or a similar process as a uniform dispersion retained after processing.
Sliding exposes CaF2 particles at the contact surface.
Exposure of CaF2 particles promotes formation of an in situ CaF2-based tribofilm.
The resulting tribofilm provides a continuous low-shear interface.
The CaF2-based tribofilm prevents adhesive or direct metal-to-metal contact.
CaF2 particles act as solid lubricants by being exposed or transferred gradually to the sliding interface.
Reducing metal-to-metal contact inhibits wear-particle generation and lowers friction and wear.
The tribofilm remains stable enough to preserve contact integrity as temperature and load vary.
The CaF2-dispersed composite will have a coefficient of friction approximately 20–30% lower than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The CaF2-dispersed composite will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi consistently from room temperature through 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has increased friction and accelerated wear, particularly at elevated temperatures, because it lacks a stable self-lubricating mechanism.
The intervention is applicable in dry sliding in ambient air between room temperature and 800 °C under moderate-to-high loads.
Aggressive oxidation may limit the effectiveness of the CaF2 intervention.
Loss of matrix mechanical cohesion caused by the CaF2 dispersion may limit the intervention's effectiveness.
